excerpt: Workpay is a Nairobi-based payroll, HR and Employer of Record platform for companies with teams across Africa, backed by Y Combinator, Norrsken22 and Visa.
content:
Workpay is payroll and HR software for companies employing people in Africa. Its platform runs payroll, statutory tax and compliance filings, attendance and leave, benefits and salary payouts, and it offers payroll outsourcing and Employer of Record (EOR) services so a company can hire in a country where it has no local entity. Its website says more than 2,000 businesses use it, that it covers 54 African countries and over 50 currencies, and that it has processed payroll for 200,000+ employees.

The company is based in Nairobi, Kenya. Y Combinator's directory says it was founded in 2019 and joined YC in winter 2020, and lists Paul Kimani (cofounder and CEO) and Jackson Kibigo Kungu as founders. TechCrunch reported a $2.7 million pre-Series A in February 2023. In August 2024 TechCrunch reported a $5 million Series A led by Norrsken22 with Visa joining, alongside existing backers including Y Combinator. Workpay said it would spend the money on financial services for employees, AI features for performance management and hiring.

Workpay does not publish a price list. Its site asks companies to book a discovery call for a quote. Workpay is most relevant to employers with staff in Kenya and other African markets, where payroll rules, statutory deductions and payout methods such as mobile money differ from country to country. Global employers comparing it with Deel or Remote should check which countries Workpay covers with its own entities and which through partners.

We have not used Workpay for this page. It brings together Workpay's own website and the reporting linked under Sources, and says where each fact comes from. Nothing here is paid placement.
